thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Sink Lower as Trump Tweets Fan Trade War Flames Anew

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Sink Lower as Trump Tweets Fan Trade War Flames Anew
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Friday's regular session:
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): +3.9%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.04%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.19%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.1%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -0.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were weaker. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 0.1%.
US stocks were marginally lower at session's half with the defensive tone fueled by the impending Group of Seven meeting in Canada and reports of lackluster demand for Apple (AAPL) iPhones.
Investor appetite for risk soured overnight when President Donald Trump's confrontational tweets targeted at France and Canada inflamed fears of a trade war between the US, Europe and Canada.
In economic data news, US wholesale inventories edged up 0.1 in April, with sales up 0.8%. March inventories posted a 0.2% gain, with sales 0.4% higher.
Power Play: Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.4% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.2%.
TapImmune (TPIV) shares surged more than 71% at one point even after the clinical-stage immuno-oncology company announced private placement of 17.5 million common shares at $4 per share, 32.8% lower than the share closing price on Thursday. Investors will also receive five-year warrants to purchase up to 13.125 million shares at $5, the company said in a statement. The transaction should close by the end of next quarter.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up marginally. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 0.6% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 0.4%.
GAIN Capital Holdings' (GCAP) over-the-counter (OTC) trading volume rose 10.8% year-over-year in May to $243.3 billion while the OTC average daily volume increased 16.8% from a year ago to $11.1 billion. For the company's futures segment, the number of contracts traded increased 31.5% from May 2017 to $694.5 billion with the average daily contracts traded also up by 31.5% to $31.57 billion. GCAP shares were down 0.7%.
Energy
Dow Jones U.S. Energy Fund (IYE) was down 0.5% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.4%.
Nordic American Tankers (NAT) fell 1% after it said in a letter to investors that it had agreed to sell three more Suezmax vessels. The agreement follows the sale of two ships previously announced on May 30. The company said that the total cash from the sales of the five vessels was close to $50 million.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.2% while other tech funds iShares Dow Jones U.S. Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were weaker.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 0.6% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 0.1%.
Cemtrex (CETX) jumped nearly 6% after it said it will hold a demonstration for its advanced work station SmarkDesk for investors in the New York City area. The company said this is in response to overwhelming interest in the product at the 8th Annual LD Micro Invitational Conference.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.7%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.3%. Natural gas was down 1.5% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.3%.
Gold was down 0.02%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.2%. Silver was down 0.2%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.1%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 1% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were firmer.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 0.2% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in positive territory.
Stitch Fix (SFIX) shares rose more than 19% after the company's announcement Thursday that it swung to a profit of $9.5 million, or $0.09 per diluted share in its fiscal Q3 ended April 28, from a net loss of $9.6 million, or $0.38 per share a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by Capital IQ had expected earnings of $0.03 per share. The online apparel and accessories seller said revenue rose to $316.7 million in the quarter from 245.1 million, also beating consensus estimates of $306.7 million.
